pr.title: Convert moves of references to copies in ReferencePropagation
pr.description:
This is a fix for https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/141101.

The root cause of this miscompile is that the SsaLocals analysis that MIR transforms use is supposed to detect locals that are only written to once, in their single assignment. But that analysis is subtly wrong; it does not consider `Operand::Move` to be a write even though the meaning ascribed to `Operand::Move` (at least as a function parameter) by Miri is that the callee may have done arbitrary writes to the caller's Local that the Operand wraps (because `Move` is pass-by-pointer). So Miri conwiders `Operand::Move` to be a write but both the MIR visitor system considers it a read, and so does SsaLocals.

I have tried fixing this by changing the `PlaceContext` that is ascribed to an `Operand::Move` to a `MutatingUseContext` but that seems to have borrow checker implications, and changing SsaLocals seems to have wide-ranging regressions in MIR optimizations.

So instead of doing those, this PR adds a new kludge to ReferencePropagation, which follows the same line of thinking as the kludge in CopyProp that solves this same problem inside that pass: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/a5584a8fe16037dc01782064fa41424a6dbe9987/compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/copy_prop.rs#L65-L98
pr.author: saethlin

analysis.summary: Historical ReferencePropagation miscompile fix: before this PR the pass ran SSA propagation directly while SsaLocals treated Operand::Move as a read, so a pointer/reference local moved into a call could still be treated as available for reference propagation. The fix preprocesses the body to turn pointer-typed Operand::Move into Operand::Copy before the SSA loop, because Move is pass-by-pointer and the callee may write through/overwrite the moved local. Non-pointer moves are left unchanged.
analysis.originalLogic: ReferencePropagation::run_pass previously just ran `while propagate_ssa(tcx, body) {}`, and `propagate_ssa` built `SsaLocals` and then `compute_replacement`. The PR states: "The SSA analysis done by [`SsaLocals`] treats [`Operand::Move`] as a read, even though in general [`Operand::Move`] represents pass-by-pointer where the callee can overwrite the pointee". Thus the pass trusted SSA single-assignment information even when a pointer/reference local was passed with Operand::Move, and could propagate/reuse that local's reference value without treating the move as invalidating it.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation was to leave `Operand::Move` of a pointer/reference in place and let SsaLocals treat it as a pure read, so ReferencePropagation could reuse/propagate the moved pointer/reference local's value across or after that move. That is unsound because the PR explains that with Move "the callee may have done arbitrary writes to the caller's Local that the Operand wraps (because `Move` is pass-by-pointer)" and "Miri always considers the place deinitialized". The fix instead rewrites every pointer-typed move to a copy before SSA analysis: `if place.ty(self.local_decls, self.tcx).ty.is_any_ptr() { *operand = Operand::Copy(place); }`, so the local is copied and stays valid rather than being assumed reusable after a move.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies containing an `Operand::Move` whose place type satisfies `is_any_ptr()`, i.e. pointer/reference-like operands (the updated dumps include `&u32`, `&mut usize`, `*const T`, `*mut T`, and other pointer values), with a later read or alias of that local or its pointee. The regression specifically uses a custom-MIR body with `_6 = _5; _7 = _6; ... Call(n = opaque(_2.1, Move(_6)), ReturnTo(bb1), UnwindUnreachable())` followed by `_2.0 = *_7;`. Moves of non-pointer types are outside the changed transformation.
analysis.trigger: ReferencePropagation runs on a body where a pointer/reference local is used as `Operand::Move` and SsaLocals considers that local to be SSA/single-assignment available for propagation; a later use/alias of the moved local or its pointee exists, possibly after an opaque call that can overwrite through the moved pointer.
preconditions: The ReferencePropagation MIR pass executes on the body.
An Operand::Move wraps a place whose type is a pointer/reference according to `is_any_ptr()`.
SsaLocals classifies the move as a read, so the moved local remains eligible for SSA-based reference propagation/reuse.
There is a later read or alias of the moved local or its pointee, optionally after a call that may write through the moved pointer.
pitfalls: Do not model this as a general SsaLocals fix: the PR explicitly avoids changing SsaLocals because that 'seems to have wide-ranging regressions in MIR optimizations'.
Changing the PlaceContext of Operand::Move to a MutatingUseContext is not the chosen fix and 'seems to have borrow checker implications'.
Operand::Move is semantically significant for pointers: it is pass-by-pointer and Miri treats the place as deinitialized, even though the MIR visitor system and SsaLocals treat it as a read.
The fix is gated by `is_any_ptr()`, so only pointer/reference moves are converted; do not generalize to all moves or expect non-pointer `move` operands to become `copy`.

Many GVN/SimplifyLocals test dumps in the patch change `move` to `copy`, but the code change is in ReferencePropagation; do not attribute this behavior to GVN or SimplifyLocals as the transforming pass.

Copying a reference changes ownership/liveness reasoning relative to moving it; the justification here is that 'pointers should be by-value anyway', not that move and copy are universally interchangeable.
analysis.testStrategy: Use a focused MIR pass test declared with `//@ test-mir-pass: ReferencePropagation`. Construct a custom-MIR body that assigns a reference local, aliases it, passes the local via `Move(...)` to an `#[inline(never)] fn opaque` call, then reads through the alias after the call. Check that ReferencePropagation rewrites the call operand to `copy` rather than `move`, as in the new regression's `// CHECK: _9 = opaque::<&u8, &u64>(copy (_2.1: &u8), copy _6)`. Complement this with the existing `reference_prop` MIR dumps for `&T`, `&mut T`, `*const T`, and `*mut T`, and update downstream GVN/SimplifyLocals dump expectations. For a differential pair, compile/run the same body once with the move-to-copy preprocessing disabled and once enabled, differing only in whether `Operand::Move(pointer_place)` remains a move or becomes `Operand::Copy(pointer_place)`; compare the resulting MIR and avoid claiming runtime reproduction since no compiler was built.
